questions.q: What does 'business-conformed' mean in the context of the marts layer?
options: Data shaped by what the business actually means by a concept, like 'an order,' rather than by the source system that produced it
Data that has been approved by the finance department specifically
Data stored in exactly the same shape as the raw source table
Data that has been deleted after being used once
questions.explain: The staging-to-marts arc moves data from source-conformed to business-conformed, and marts are where that arc ends.

questions.q: Why are marts models deliberately wide and denormalized?
options: Storage is cheap and compute is expensive, so precomputing columns once at the mart saves everyone downstream from re-deriving the same logic
dbt requires every mart to have at least 50 columns
Wide tables are the only materialization type dbt supports
Normalization is not possible in a cloud data warehouse
questions.explain: Marts pack in computed columns like order costs and boolean flags on purpose, absorbing the compute cost once instead of many times downstream.

questions.q: Which of these is an explicit marts-layer naming anti-pattern?
options: Creating both a finance_orders and a marketing_orders mart describing the same underlying entity
Naming a mart 'customers' after the entity it represents
Materializing a mart as a table once query performance degrades
Referencing an intermediate model inside a mart
questions.explain: Departmental duplicates of the same entity are exactly the drift the marts layer is designed to prevent — one orders mart, used by everyone.

questions.q: How does mart materialization typically evolve as a project grows?
options: View, then table once query performance degrades, then incremental once the build itself becomes too expensive
Table, then view, then ephemeral, in that fixed order
It never changes — marts are always materialized as views
Marts must be materialized as snapshots from day one
questions.explain: That progression is deliberate — don't pay for infrastructure (like incremental logic) a project doesn't need yet.

questions.q: According to this lesson's naming guidance, what's wrong with naming a mart 'orders_per_day'?
options: It names the mart after a time rollup / metric rather than the entity itself
The name is too short for dbt to parse correctly
dbt reserves that name for internal use
It violates the 1-to-1 rule that only applies to staging models
questions.explain: Time-based rollups describe a metric, not an entity — that kind of aggregation belongs in a query or semantic layer, not the mart's name.
